en.title: Signals That Pass All Frequency Filters
en.description:
Each closed-interval filter lets through only frequencies inside its interval. Find the number of input signals that pass every filter; repeated frequencies count as separate signals. All filters are guaranteed to share a common range.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: The first line contains n m, the second line contains n frequencies, followed by m lines of lower upper; 1≤n,m≤100000, and frequencies and endpoints are in 1..1000000000.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 2; 2; 0. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: The intersection's lower bound is the maximum of all lower bounds and its upper bound is the minimum of all upper bounds; count the signals that fall inside it.
